- Overestimate prices when sentiment is positive (especially >0.23) — model tends to lag or overshoot upward momentum.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative (especially < -0.16) — model fails to capture downward pressure or mean reversion.
- Overshoot after sharp sentiment spikes (e.g., +0.61) — model overreacts and peaks too early.
- Underreact to sustained negative sentiment — model holds too close to prior levels, missing downward drift.
- Mean reversion bias: model often overcorrects after strong moves, especially in 30-day horizon.
- Lag in response to recent sentiment shifts — model takes 2–3 days to adjust after sentiment changes direction.
- Avoid overfitting to recent highs — if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative, model still forecasts upward, leading to overestimation.
- Price correction is delayed when sentiment is volatile — model doesn’t fully absorb sentiment volatility in 30-day forecast.
